props.gloss_en: at first women were inside and men outside, and they came to levity
they enacted that women sit outside and men inside, and still they came to levity
they enacted that women sit above and men below
but it is written: 'all this in writing from the hand of the Lord upon me' (I Chr 28:19) -- the Temple's plan was given in writing
Rav: they found a verse and expounded it
'and the land shall mourn, each family apart; the family of the house of David apart, and their women apart' (Zech 12:12) -- at the future eulogy men and women are apart
now, when they are occupied with rejoicing and the evil inclination rules them, all the more so [men and women apart]
one said: [the eulogy is] for Mashiach ben Yosef who was killed
and one said: for the evil inclination that was killed
that is what is written: 'and they shall look to Me, whom they pierced, and mourn for him as one mourns an only son' (Zech 12:10)
should one make a eulogy for this? one should make a rejoicing! why did they weep?
R' Yehuda: in the future God brings the evil inclination and slaughters it before the righteous and before the wicked
to the righteous it appears like a high mountain
to the wicked it appears like a strand of hair
both weep: the righteous -- how were we able to conquer so high a mountain; the wicked -- how were we unable to conquer this hair
and God too wonders with them
as it is said: 'if it be wondrous in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, it shall also be wondrous in My eyes' (Zech 8:6)
Rav Asi: the evil inclination at first is like a spider's thread and in the end like wagon ropes
as it is said: 'woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as with wagon ropes' (Isa 5:18)
to Mashiach ben David God says: ask of Me anything and I will give it to you
as it is said: 'I will tell of the decree... this day I have begotten you; ask of Me and I will give the nations as your inheritance' (Ps 2:7-8)
seeing Mashiach ben Yosef killed, he asks only for life; God: before you said it, David your father already prophesied it of you
as it is said: 'he asked life of You, You gave it him' (Ps 21:5)
the evil inclination has seven names
God called it 'evil' -- 'for the inclination of man's heart is evil from his youth' (Gen 8:21)
Moses called it 'uncircumcised' -- 'circumcise the foreskin of your heart' (Deut 10:16)
David called it 'impure' -- 'create in me a pure heart, O God' (Ps 51:12), by implication there is an impure one
Solomon called it 'enemy' -- 'if your enemy hungers, feed him bread... and the Lord will reward you' (Prov 25:21-22); read not 'reward you' but 'make him at peace with you'
Isaiah called it 'stumbling block' -- 'remove the stumbling block from the way of My people' (Isa 57:14)
Ezekiel called it 'stone' -- 'I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh' (Ezek 36:26)
Joel called it 'the northern/hidden one' -- 'and I will remove the northern one far from you' (Joel 2:20)
'the northern one' -- this is the evil inclination, which is hidden in a person's heart
'and I will drive it to a dry and desolate land' -- to a place where there are no people for it to incite
'its face toward the eastern sea' -- it set its eyes on the First Temple, destroyed it, and killed its Torah scholars
'and its end toward the western sea' -- it set its eyes on the Second Temple, destroyed it, and killed its Torah scholars
'its stench shall rise' -- it leaves the nations of the world and incites 'the enemies of Israel'
'for it has done great things' -- Abaye: and against Torah scholars more than all
Abaye heard a man tell a woman 'let us rise early and go on the road'; he followed them three parasangs through the marsh; parting, they said 'the road was long and the company pleasant'
Abaye: had it been 'one who hates me' [himself], he could not have restrained himself
the elder: whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his
R' Yitzchak: a person's inclination overpowers him every day
as it is said: 'only evil all the day' (Gen 6:5)
Resh Lakish: a person's inclination overpowers him every day and seeks to kill him
as it is said: 'the wicked watches the righteous and seeks to kill him' (Ps 37:32)
and were it not that God helps him, he could not withstand it
as it is said: 'the Lord will not leave him in its hand' (Ps 37:33)
if this repulsive one meets you, drag it to the study hall
if it is stone it dissolves -- 'ho, all who thirst, come to the water' (Isa 55:1) and 'water wears away stones' (Job 14:19)
if it is iron it shatters -- 'is not My word like fire, and like a hammer that shatters rock' (Jer 23:29)
the evil inclination incites a person in this world and testifies against him in the world to come
as it is said: 'he who pampers his servant from youth, in the end he shall be manon' (Prov 29:21); in R' Chiyya's atbach, a witness is called manon
Rav Huna set 'a spirit of harlotry led them astray' (Hos 4:12) against '[a spirit of harlotry] is within them' (Hos 5:4): at first it leads them astray, in the end it is within them
Rava: at first it is called a traveller, then a guest, and at last a man [of the house]
as it is said: 'there came a traveller to the rich man... to prepare for the guest... and prepared it for the man who had come to him' (II Sam 12:4)
R' Yochanan: a man has a small organ; starve it and it is sated, sate it and it is hungry
as it is said: 'when they were fed they were sated...' (Hos 13:6)
four things God regrets having created: exile, the Chaldeans, the Ishmaelites, and the evil inclination
exile -- 'and now what have I here, says the Lord, that My people is taken away for nothing' (Isa 52:5)
the Chaldeans -- 'behold the land of the Chaldeans, this people was not' (Isa 23:13)
the Ishmaelites -- 'the tents of robbers are at ease... whom God brought into His hand' (Job 12:6)
the evil inclination -- 'and her whom I have harmed' (Mic 4:6)

R' Yochanan: were it not for these three verses -- 'and her whom I have harmed' (Mic 4:6), 'as clay in the potter's hand' (Jer 18:6), 'I will remove the heart of stone' (Ezek 36:26) -- the feet of 'the enemies of Israel' would have given way
Rav Pappa: also from this: 'and I will put My spirit within you...' (Ezek 36:27)
'the Lord showed me four craftsmen' (Zech 2:3) -- Mashiach ben David, Mashiach ben Yosef, Elijah, and the righteous priest
'and he said to me: these are the horns that scattered Judah' (Zech 2) -- these came for good!
go down to the end of the verse: 'these have come to terrify them, to cast down the horns of the nations that lifted up a horn against the land of Judah to scatter it' (Zech 2:4)
Rav Sheshet: why should I [contend] with Chana in aggada?
who are the seven shepherds (Mic 5:4)? David in the middle; Adam, Seth and Methuselah on his right; Abraham, Jacob and Moses on his left
who are the eight princes of men? Jesse, Saul, Samuel, Amos, Zephaniah, Zedekiah, Mashiach, and Elijah
